title: Introduce cost-ops rulebook and quant tier prober
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/quant profiles manually. We need an automated, auditable rulebook that derives tenant-safe defaults and a probing binary (quant-tier-prober) that runs lightweight on Dedicated/Private to surface unit-econ tradeoffs and safe fallbacks. This PR delivers: 1) a cost-ops rulebook data model and evaluator (deterministic, policy-driven) that encodes tenant constraints, SLO targets and preferred cost bands; 2) a quant-tier-prober CLI to run controlled micro-benchmarks and produce recommended quantization tiers and fallback maps; 3) a small orchestration shim that wires prober outputs into the defaults compiler used by the tenant provisioning flow; 4) docs and an integration test harness. The description below is a single continuous string but includes sections: Design highlights: - Rulebook is JSON/YAML-first with versioning and drift detection. Rules express cost targets (per-1k tokens), max-latency p50/p95, quality budget (relative metric), and allowed quant tiers per-model-family. - Prober runs three phases: micro-latency sweep, sample-inference quality probe using canned prompts, and safety validation (compare logits/embeddings distance against baseline thresholds). - Outputs: quant-recommendation.yaml (per-tenant, per-model), safe-fallback-map (mapping high-quant -> compatible lower-quant variant), and a compact telemetry bundle for Console ingestion. Backwards compatibility: the rulebook evaluator supports a legacy fallback path that emits 'no-op' defaults for tenants that opt out. Checklist: - [x] rulebook schema, evaluator, CLI - [x] quant-tier-prober binary and Dockerfile - [x] integration tests (simulated Dedicated environment) - [x] docs: cost-ops rulebook guide and troubleshooting - [x] CI smoke tests and a flakiness guard (re-run on known flaky tests) Risk and mitigations: - Quality regressions: prober uses a conservative default threshold (0.95 similarity) and refuses to recommend changes without at least 3 repeatable samples. - Safety in production: recommendations are rollouts only; we wire outputs into the existing canary/AB rollout pipeline (no immediate tenant flips). Related: ENG-1987 (cost automation roadmap), ENG-2031 (quant-safety metrics).
commits: 1) init: add cost-ops rulebook types and evaluator; 2) add quant-tier-prober core sweeper and quality probe; 3) integrate prober outputs into defaults-compiler; 4) add e2e test for prober flow and sample artifacts; 5) docs and examples; 6) CI: add prober job and caching; commit messages kept small and focused
